skill.name: github-pr-merge
skill.description: Guides GitHub pull request merges with validation checks, user confirmation, merge message formatting, and branch cleanup steps.
skill.summary: Validate, confirm, merge, and clean up GitHub pull requests with a consistent checklist.
skill.author: Bae-ChangHyun

security_audit.summary: The skill is a GitHub PR merge workflow that intentionally uses gh, git, and make commands. Most static hits are Markdown or read-only GitHub CLI checks, but merge, branch deletion, and repository-defined make targets are real risks. The frontmatter also contains prompt override wording that should be softened before marketplace publication.

remediation.issue: Prompt override language in skill metadata
remediation.suggestion: Replace mandatory and override wording with neutral activation guidance, such as using the skill for requested PR merge workflows.

remediation.issue: High-impact merge and remote branch deletion command
remediation.suggestion: Require an explicit PR number, show the target repository and branch, and ask for separate confirmation before deleting any branch.

remediation.issue: Repository-defined make targets execute local code
remediation.suggestion: Document that validation commands should run only in trusted workspaces, or ask before running project-controlled commands.

remediation.issue: Shell variables are not consistently quoted in examples
remediation.suggestion: Quote PR and repository variables in shell examples and validate that the PR value is numeric before use.

content.value_statement: Pull request merges need consistent validation before repository changes happen. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through checks, confirmation, merge, and cleanup.
actual_capabilities: Identifies the current pull request and repository with GitHub CLI commands.
Checks tests, lint, CI status, and review comment replies before merge.
Guides explicit user confirmation before executing a merge command.
Formats concise merge messages with review and test summaries.
Describes post-merge cleanup for develop branch sync and local branch deletion.
limitations: Requires GitHub CLI, authenticated access, git, and project validation commands.
Cannot resolve failing tests, lint, CI, or unreplied review comments.
Assumes the repository uses a develop branch and make targets.
Includes commands that merge pull requests and delete branches.

use_cases.title: Complete a reviewed feature merge
use_cases.description: Validate checks, summarize readiness, and merge after explicit approval.

use_cases.title: Verify review comments before merge
use_cases.description: Check whether original review comments have replies before accepting a pull request.

use_cases.title: Prepare an assistant-guided merge
use_cases.description: Ask an AI coding assistant to collect status, draft the merge summary, and wait for approval.
use_cases.target_user: Developer using Claude, Codex, or Claude Code

prompt_templates.title: Check the Current PR
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner workflow for a normal pull request merge.
prompt_templates.prompt: Check the current GitHub pull request. Run the required validation steps, summarize the results, and ask me before merging.

prompt_templates.title: Verify Review Readiness
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate workflow when review comments may still need attention.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the current PR for test, lint, CI, and comment status. Tell me whether anything blocks the merge.

prompt_templates.title: Merge a Specific PR
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow with an explicit pull request number.
prompt_templates.prompt: For PR #123, verify CI, tests, lint, and review comments. Prepare the merge body, then wait for my approval.

prompt_templates.title: Merge and Clean Up
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow that includes post-merge branch cleanup.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the GitHub PR merge workflow for PR #123. Validate every gate, merge only after my confirmation, then prepare cleanup steps.

output_examples.input: Merge the current PR after checking it.
output: PR #42 is ready: tests passed, lint passed, CI is green, and review comments are answered.
Merge message drafted with key changes, review count, and test summary. Waiting for your confirmation before merge.

output_examples.input: Check whether this PR can merge.
output_examples.output: The merge is blocked because two review comments have no replies. Run the review workflow before merging.

output_examples.input: After merge, clean up my branch.
output_examples.output: The remote branch can be deleted during merge. Local branch cleanup should happen only after switching to the target branch and pulling updates.

best_practices: Confirm the PR number and repository before running any merge command.
Treat project validation commands as repository code and run them only in trusted workspaces.
Keep branch deletion as a separate decision when the branch is shared.
anti_patterns: Do not merge when tests, lint, CI, or review threads are unresolved.
Do not use the skill to bypass branch protection or reviewer approval.
Do not run merge commands from a fork or untrusted checkout without verifying context.

faq.question: Does this skill merge automatically?
faq.answer: No. It instructs the assistant to ask for explicit confirmation before merging.

faq.question: What tools are required?
faq.answer: It requires GitHub CLI, git, authentication to the target repository, and the project validation commands.

faq.question: Can it respond to review comments?
faq.answer: No. The workflow says to stop and use a review workflow when unreplied comments exist.

faq.question: Does it support squash merges?
faq.answer: The skill recommends merge commits only. Adjust the workflow manually if project policy differs.

faq.question: Why does it check comments?
faq.answer: It checks comment replies to reduce the chance of merging unresolved review feedback.

faq.question: Is it safe for untrusted repositories?
faq.answer: Use caution. Project validation commands can execute repository-defined code on the local machine.
